topic.title: Class Imbalance and Long-Tailed Recognition
topic.overview: When some classes appear far more often than others, optimizing average training loss can leave rare classes poorly modeled. This topic studies margins, weighting, resampling, logit adjustment, and representation geometry for imbalanced learning. A central issue is aligning the training objective with the evaluation priorities rather than treating observed frequency as universal importance.
topic.whyItMatters: Improving minority-class performance may change overall accuracy, calibration, or group behavior. Methods therefore need clear targets and suitable evaluation, especially when rare classes also have few reliable examples. Rebalancing can affect representation learning differently from the final classifier, making training schedules consequential.
topic.evolution: Representative titles from 1997 address minority prediction and selection of imbalanced training data. LDAM in 2019 uses class-sensitive margins and studies delayed reweighting. Later work analyzes reweighting and logit adjustment together; a 2026 approach treats reweighting as an inverse problem aimed at equalizing per-class losses under a neural-collapse-inspired objective.
openQuestions: Which balancing targets remain useful when test-time class frequencies are unknown?
How can rare-class improvements be distinguished from overfitting a small evaluation sample?

papers.tldr: MORE improves recognition of rare classes by rebalancing model parameters without increasing overall complexity or inference cost.

papers.title: LT-Soups: Bridging Head and Tail Classes via Subsampled Model Soups
papers.tldr: LT-Soups averages models trained on balanced subsets, then adjusts the classifier to improve accuracy trade-offs between common and rare classes.

papers.title: QuanDA: Quantile-Based Discriminant Analysis for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Classification
papers.tldr: QuanDA uses quantile-based discriminant analysis to address class imbalance in small-sample, high-dimensional classification.

papers.title: Sampled Estimators For Softmax Must Be Biased
papers.tldr: The paper proves that estimators accessing only a sampled subset of classes cannot avoid bias when estimating softmax.

papers.title: Stratify or Die: Rethinking Data Splits in Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: Label-aware segmentation splits, especially WDES, yield more representative evaluations and lower performance variance in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Thumb on the Scale: Optimal Loss Weighting in Last Layer Retraining
papers.tldr: Loss weighting can improve class balance in last-layer retraining, but its weights must reflect relative model overparameterization.

papers.title: TS-MOF: Two-Stage Multi-Objective Fine-tuning for Long-Tailed Recognition
papers.tldr: TS-MOF freezes pretrained features and coordinates classifier objectives to improve both common and rare class recognition.

papers.title: When majority rules, minority loses: bias amplification of gradient descent
papers.tldr: Under population and variance imbalance, a theoretical framework shows how training can favor majority traits and neglect minority-specific features.

papers.title: Class-Conditional Distribution Balancing for Group Robust Classification
papers.tldr: The paper improves robust classification by reweighting examples to balance class-conditional distributions without requiring explicit bias labels or predictions.

papers.title: CSOR: Coreset Selection for Object Re-identification via Class Pruning
papers.tldr: CSOR builds better re-identification training subsets by pruning low-diversity classes and selecting examples that cover variation within the remaining classes.

papers.title: GFD-EMVC: Evolutionary Multi-View Classification with Label Noise via Gradient and Feature Dual-Perception
papers.tldr: GFD-EMVC detects suspicious labels through gradient outliers and corrects them using feature prototypes to improve learning and evolutionary search.

papers.title: Instance-Level Costs for Nuanced Classifier Evaluation
papers.tldr: Normalized excess cost weights classification mistakes by example-specific costs, revealing distinctions that ordinary error rates can hide.

papers.title: Let the Prototype Guide You: Robust Aggregation of Sparse Multi-Class Annotations via Annotator Prototype Learning
papers.tldr: CPBCC shares class-specific annotation prototypes across annotators to improve label aggregation under sparse data and complex labeling behavior.

papers.title: LOTTERY: Learning from Reference-Only Samples in Two-Sample Testing under Size Asymmetry
papers.tldr: LOTTERY learns and weights representations from abundant reference data to support two-sample testing with very few query samples.

papers.title: Negatives-Dominant Contrastive Learning for Generalization in Imbalanced Domains
papers.tldr: NDCL emphasizes negative contrastive examples and prediction alignment to improve generalization across domains with uneven class frequencies.

papers.title: Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings
papers.tldr: MILD reformulates expert routing as cost-sensitive learning to improve deferral when expert imbalance biases existing methods.

papers.title: Rethinking Loss Reweighting for Imbalance Learning as an Inverse Problem: A Neural Collapse Point of View
papers.tldr: The paper dynamically infers class weights to approach equal per-class average loss, improving long-tailed classification in its experiments.

papers.title: Risk-Bounded Distribution Reconstruction: Stable Statistic Calibration for Long-Tailed Recognition
papers.tldr: RBDR controls mean and covariance updates for rare classes to improve reconstruction stability and class separation.

papers.title: When Softmax Fails at the Top: Extreme-Value Corrections for InfoNCE
papers.tldr: WEINCE adds a parameter-free extreme-value correction to InfoNCE and improves frozen-feature evaluation across five vision benchmarks.
